_v1_notes.CONTRABAND|CONCEALMENT: sanctioned machinery is too large to bury in cargo or hide in a cavity - it is a documentation offence, so falsified manifest and seal swap only. Narcotics and cash are N for falsified manifest alone: nobody declares them under any description. Counterfeit goods fill the container, so a structural cavity is N.
_v1_notes.CONTRABAND|FACILITATOR: a freight forwarder controls documents only, so is N for narcotics and cash, which need physical concealment rather than a description. Machinery is N for a crane operator and a ship's officer - moving a box does not solve a paperwork offence - and Y for the inspector and forwarder.
_v1_notes.CONTRABAND|DETECTION METHOD: canine search detects only narcotics. X-ray is N for machinery (declared openly, nothing anomalous) and N for counterfeit goods (radiographically identical to genuine).
_v1_notes.CONCEALMENT|FACILITATOR: a crane operator has no documentation access, so is N for burying in cargo and N for a falsified manifest; a seal swap is precisely their contribution. A ship's officer has no terminal or customs access, so N for manifest falsification and N for a seal swap. A forwarder has no physical access, so N for cargo burial and N for seal swap.
_v1_notes.CONCEALMENT|DETECTION METHOD: a falsified manifest is invisible to X-ray, dogs and devanning of goods that are genuinely present - only analytics catches it. A structural cavity is not odour-bearing so canine is N, and analytics sees nothing wrong in the paperwork so N. Cargo burial is invisible to analytics.
_v1_notes.FACILITATOR|DETECTION METHOD: a crane operator's seal swap defeats X-ray, dogs and analytics because the inspection already happened - only devanning at destination catches it. A forwarder's offence is documentary, invisible to X-ray, dogs and devanning. A ship's officer's stowage choice is invisible to analytics.
